clue.text: Fed with soups or stews? Healthy stuff

indicators.note: to stew things is to cook them together into a mess, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether eating soups or stews counts as nourishing food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed with soups or stews' reads as a meal, but stews is a verb telling you to mix FED SOUPS OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Superfoods are foods marketed as especially nutritious, so they are healthy stuff to eat.

clue.text: Bar or shaft with half of it missing

indicators.note: missing means the named letter is left out

parts.note: a stave is a staff or wooden shaft

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word it is its second letter

parts.note: the word it has two letters, and the second half of it is removed

explanation.surface: A bar or rod with half its length gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' seems to refer to the shaft, but it is the word it, half of which is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Save as a preposition means except, as does bar: everyone bar one.

clue.text: Study risk if Italy's replaced by America

indicators.note: replaced by means the letter for Italy is swapped out for the American letters

parts.note: peril is danger or risk
I is Italy's international vehicle code
USA, the United States of America

explanation.surface: An analysis of risk if America took Italy's place.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination, a study of something.

clue.text: Evidence of fare in bar means instant eats on a regular basis

parts.note: a rail is a bar
a way is a means of doing something
a tick is a moment or instant

indicators.note: on a regular basis means every other letter of eats is taken

parts.note: the first and third letters of eats are kept

explanation.surface: Proof of what food is like in a bar where snacks are served instantly and regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests food, matching eats; it is the price of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway ticket proves that the passenger has paid the fare for the journey.

clue.text: I will probe zero cost of hiring from China?

indicators.note: to probe is to poke into, so the letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a rental is the charge for hiring something
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to investigate a nil charge for hiring something from China.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things from East Asia, of which China is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Active person on vacation daringly upheld Arab state

indicators.note: vacated, a word keeps only its outside letters, its inside emptied

parts.note: only the first and last letters of daringly remain once it is emptied

indicators.note: upheld in a down clue means lifted up, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: An energetic traveller on holiday boldly supporting a Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a forceful, energetic person, after the electrical generator.

clue.text: Introduction being missing from explanation could be considered this

definitions.text: Introduction being missing from explanation could be considered this

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter, which is taken away here

parts.note: a gloss is an explanatory note on a text

explanation.surface: A comment that an explanation lacking its opening would be deficient.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: losing the first letter of the gloss is itself a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Having part of something go missing is a deprivation, which is what the word names.

clue.text: Criminal 4, not European, facing court

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are rearranged
not means the European letter is left out

parts.note: the answer to clue 4, ORIENTAL

explanation.surface: A criminal, not from Europe, appearing before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on trial is facing a court hearing to decide guilt.

clue.text: Conceal outlay involving large part of Hollywood feature

parts.note: to screen is to hide or conceal

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the large letter goes inside the outlay word

parts.note: pay is money laid out

explanation.surface: Hiding the large budget that went into a Hollywood movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large part' looks like one phrase, but large gives its letter and 'part of Hollywood feature' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay is the script of a film, one component of a feature film.

clue.text: I noted part of clever diagram

definitions.text: I noted part of clever diagram

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the run of letters in these two words

parts.note: the end of clever and the start of diagram run together to spell the composer

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that they spotted a detail in a smart chart.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as the composer speaking: 'I noted', a composer writing notes, and his name sits inside clever diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the celebrated Italian opera composer, a man who wrote down musical notes.

clue.text: Pub adding eggs to beer, ultimately the source of a good idea

definitions.text: the source of a good idea

indicators.note: adding puts the following pieces after the pub, building the word along

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ova is Latin for eggs, the biological plural
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word beer

parts.note: the last letter of beer

explanation.surface: A pub's brainwave of mixing eggs into beer, credited as a source of invention.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovator is someone who comes up with new methods and ideas, an originator.

clue.text: Worsening situation here in France, stopping you, in Paris, meeting group of friends

indicators.note: meeting joins the next piece on after the first
stopping means plugging up, so the French here goes into the French you

parts.note: vous is French for you
ici is French for here
a circle is a social group

explanation.surface: A visitor in France getting stuck while meeting a group of friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicious circle is a cycle in which each problem makes the next one worse.

clue.text: One uses a pedal when cycling from Beijing, perhaps, with flight before noon pushed back

indicators.note: the flight and morning pieces go along with the cycled word, set within it
cycling moves the closing letters of the word round to the front

parts.note: Beijing is an example of something Chinese, the capital city
a wing is a flight or division of an air force

indicators.note: pushed back means the two letters are put in reverse order

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is the time before noon

explanation.surface: A cyclist pedalling away from Beijing, having caught a morning flight that was delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedal' and 'cycling' paint a bicycle, but the pedal is a treadle, and cycling moves SE of CHINESE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Many sewing machines are driven by a foot treadle, a pedal that controls the speed of stitching.

clue.text: Uphill motorway not that good? Blocked entirely

indicators.note: uphill in a down clue means reading from bottom to top, reversing the letters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, its digit read as the letter I
passable means adequate, not especially good

explanation.surface: A road going uphill that is mediocre and completely closed.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; the digit 1 stands in for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassable means impossible to travel through, so wholly blocked.

clue.text: Galaxy exploit — cry of joy with wife coming aboard

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it

indicators.note: coming aboard means getting inside, so the wife letter goes into the cry

parts.note: yay is an exclamation of delight

explanation.surface: Someone celebrating with a whoop as their wife joins them on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Galaxy is also a chocolate brand, as is Milky Way, which adds to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Milky Way is the galaxy containing our solar system, the spiral of stars seen across the night sky.

clue.text: Party twisted vote a vague amount

parts.note: a do is a party or social event

indicators.note: twisted here means turned round, so the word for vote is read backwards

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A political party distorting a ballot result by an unclear margin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is an imprecise lump or spoonful of something soft, a vague quantity.

clue.text: Brown loaf or cob?

parts.note: hazel is a light brown colour
loaf and nut are both slang for the head

explanation.surface: Choosing between a brown loaf and a cob, a round loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: A cob is a round loaf of bread in Britain, which matches the bakery picture; it is also a large hazelnut.
explanation.definitionFit: Cob is the name for a type of large hazelnut, also called cobnut, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Three letters encapsulating Government spies on a small scale

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so the spies go inside the three letters

parts.note: A to C spans three letters of the alphabet, A, B and C
MI, Military Intelligence, as in MI5 and MI6, the state's spy agencies

explanation.surface: A short acronym concealing a government intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three letters' is not an abbreviation but the range A TO C.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic describes things at the scale of atoms, so tiny or minute in scale.

clue.text: Loves American to implicate Democrat and Republican regarding a stink

indicators.note: to implicate is to involve or fold in, so the party letters are drawn in among the others

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero is the letter O, so loves are several Os

explanation.surface: An American scandal draws both political parties into something that smells bad.
explanation.walkthrough: D and R go in separately, after the first and second Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odorous gives off a smell, so the word concerns a stink.

clue.text: A University only brought in arts degree in locations of late?

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so these pieces go within the degree

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts
taken as written
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A university that admitted only students taking arts degrees in recent times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of late' seems to mean recently; here the late are the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Mausolea are grand tombs, the resting places of the deceased, who are 'the late'.

clue.text: Sticky stuff in residue may be vegetables

indicators.note: in means the sticky stuff sits inside the residue

parts.note: lees are the dregs left in a wine barrel
gum is a sticky substance

explanation.surface: A gooey deposit left in the dregs might turn out to be vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Legumes are pod vegetables such as peas, beans and lentils.

clue.text: Stony cairn finally reduced to rubble?

parts.note: stony broke means having no money, so stony stands for broke

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of cairn

parts.note: the last letter of cairn

explanation.surface: A pile of stones in the hills ending up as rubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stony' fits the cairn picture; it means penniless, from stony broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reduced to rubble has been smashed apart, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Conventional manners may be what's expected at some farms

parts.note: stock as an adjective means standard or conventional, as in a stock reply
good breeding means good manners

explanation.surface: A comment that traditional politeness is the norm in rural farming circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock farms raise animals, so breeding cattle and sheep is what one expects there.

clue.text: A number of horses bolt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a collection of horses kept for breeding
second meaning: a short bolt or rivet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' tempts as what horses do, running off; here it is a metal fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a breeding establishment of horses and a stout metal stud or fastener.

clue.text: Reserve acceptable among football team after dismissal? One's part of exchange deal

parts.note: to book is to reserve

indicators.note: among puts the acceptable letters in the middle of the team

parts.note: a football side is eleven; with one player sent off it is ten
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: A reserve player being brought into a football side after a sending-off, as part of a transfer deal.
explanation.walkthrough: A book token is a gift voucher exchanged in a shop for books.
explanation.definitionFit: A book token is a voucher traded in for books, so it is one side of an exchange.

clue.text: Military boss encountered historic jet

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A commanding officer coming across an old jet aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland Comet was the world's first commercial jet airliner, from the 1950s.

clue.text: Comfortable? Not comfortable, without question

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the question abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: queasy means uneasy or slightly sick

explanation.surface: Someone asked if they are comfortable answers no, without being asked twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to contradict itself; 'not comfortable' is QUEASY, which loses its question.
explanation.definitionFit: To be easy is to be relaxed and at ease, as in 'I'm easy'.

clue.text: Feeling calm, knocked back sweets and most of fruit

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: sweets are desserts, puddings

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a nut is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone relaxed after downing puddings and a lot of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests eating greedily; it reverses the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstressed means free of anxiety or tension, relaxed.
